facts.text: EMDAP is the US nuclear regulator's 20-step process for building and judging a safety-analysis model; PIRT ranks the physical phenomena that matter most; BEPU reports a best-estimate result with uncertainty rather than a single worst-case number.
facts.quote: EMDAP is the US nuclear regulator's 20-step process for building and judging a safety-analysis model, PIRT is its ranked list of the physical phenomena that matter most, and BEPU is the nuclear practice of reporting a best-estimate result with its uncertainty

facts.text: The nuclear industry developed a disciplined method for deciding when a model may be trusted because nuclear plants cannot be tested to destruction.
facts.quote: Nuclear plants cannot be tested to destruction, so the industry built a disciplined method for deciding when a model may be trusted.

facts.text: US Nuclear Regulatory Commission Regulatory Guide 1.203, dated December 2005, defines the Evaluation Model Development and Assessment Process (EMDAP) as four elements in 20 steps.
facts.quote: US Nuclear Regulatory Commission Regulatory Guide 1.203 (December 2005) defines the Evaluation Model Development and Assessment Process (EMDAP): four elements in 20 steps.

entities.name: Evaluation Model Development and Assessment Process (EMDAP)

facts.text: EMDAP Element 1 sets requirements, including a Phenomena Identification and Ranking Table (PIRT) listing every physical effect that could influence the result and ranking effects by importance and how well they are understood.
facts.quote: Element 1 sets requirements, including a Phenomena Identification and Ranking Table (PIRT): a list of every physical effect that could influence the result, ranked by importance and by how well it is understood.

facts.text: EMDAP Element 2 builds an assessment base using PIRT-selected experiments: separate-effects tests isolate one phenomenon, integral-effects tests exercise the coupled system, and scaling analysis shows that test-rig data apply to the full plant.
facts.quote: Element 2 builds the assessment base: experiments chosen with the PIRT, including separate-effects tests that isolate one phenomenon and integral-effects tests that exercise the coupled system, plus scaling analysis showing that test-rig data apply to the full plant.

facts.text: EMDAP Element 3 develops the model, and Element 4 judges model adequacy.
facts.quote: Element 3 develops the model; Element 4 judges adequacy.

facts.text: In the EMDAP process, highly ranked phenomena need test data, while low-ranked phenomena receive less emphasis.
facts.quote: Highly ranked phenomena need test data; low-ranked ones get less emphasis

facts.text: BEPU (best estimate plus uncertainty) runs the most realistic model available and reports a quantified uncertainty band instead of stacking conservative assumptions.
facts.quote: BEPU, best estimate plus uncertainty, runs the most realistic model available and reports its result with a quantified uncertainty band instead of stacking conservative assumptions.

facts.text: The booklet names BEPU and the older CSAU method but did not verify either method.
facts.quote: The booklet names BEPU and the older CSAU method but did not verify them

facts.text: Applying nuclear assessment logic to braking means testing sensor propagation, perception, latency, control logic, brake dynamics, and tire or track interaction separately, then reserving fewer full-machine tests for coupled behavior.
facts.quote: Mapped onto braking: separate sensor propagation, perception, latency, control logic, brake dynamics and tire or track interaction, test each in isolation, then reserve fewer full-machine tests for coupled behavior.

facts.text: Mapping nuclear assessment logic onto braking is not a nuclear requirement for earth-moving machinery.
facts.quote: This applies the nuclear logic; it is not a nuclear requirement for earth-moving machinery

facts.text: A PIRT-style ranking of brake fade, dust attenuation, glare, and mount vibration is on the assessor's list and determines which physical tests to keep.
facts.quote: A PIRT-style ranking (brake fade, dust attenuation, glare, mount vibration) is on the assessor's list and decides which physical tests to keep.

facts.text: A peer-reviewed criticism notes that PIRT ranking is subjective and that this subjectivity should be treated explicitly.
facts.quote: A peer-reviewed criticism notes that PIRT ranking is subjective and should be treated explicitly
